summary: A humorous feature on the producers and promoters behind a local music scene, profiling quirky figures such as Producer Pete, Sally Strummer, Barry 'Bassdrop' Bollard, Jenny Jumpstart, Terry Tune and Sarah Soundscaper. It describes their absurd events, venues, merch and gimmicks, and closes by toasting these behind-the-scenes people who shape the local sound.
one_line: A satirical tribute to local music producers and promoters, showcasing their eccentric gigs, venues, merch and events.
key_facts: Producer Pete is a pseudonym for a producer likened to the Wizard of Oz; he was working on October 13th.
Pete says he once tried to harmonize a cat with a lawnmower, and a local garage punk band adopted the result as its lead single.
On November 22nd, promoter Sally Strummer organized a gig where the audience chose the setlist via real-time online polling.
At Sally Strummer's polling gig, Free Bird was requested for the 27th time and the cover band ran out of encores, so Sally performed a spoken-word version.
Barry 'Bassdrop' Bollard turned a former fast-food joint into a music venue, using acoustic foam stuck to the walls with leftover condiments.
Bassdrop scheduled a series of events called 'Fry-days' starting in September.
Jenny Jumpstart, the 'Merch Maven', sold shirts in October that changed color depending on how much you overpaid for your drink at the bar.
The Hipster Whisperers, a group of promoters, earmarked December 1st as 'Undiscovered Band Day' to showcase obscure bands.
Terry Tune, known as 'That Illuminated Guy' since last November, uses an old television playing 'Baywatch' re-runs as stage light and matches each chord with a scent.
Sarah Soundscaper invited fans on September 9th to a live experiment where sound waves were made visible by a disco-infused fog machine.
Pasta Punk Productions organized the 'Stringless Guitar Contest' last December, won by a man who played with a tennis racket and a partridge in a pear tree.
The promoter's guiding directive is described as 'Thou Shalt Party On', explaining the existence of after-after parties.
